insider_note: This is the first of several questions on this page built from the same one formula — spot f(x) and f′(x) inside the bracket and the whole question is done in two lines.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Identify f(x) and f′(x)
steps.why: The bracket sinx+cosx is exactly f(x)+f′(x) for f(x)=sinx — recognising this pairing is the whole method for this family of questions.
common_mistakes: Trying integration by parts on eˣsinx and eˣcosx separately instead of spotting the f+f′ pairing.
Swapping the roles, taking f(x)=cosx, f′(x)=sinx — but the derivative of cosx is −sinx, not sinx, so this pairing fails the check.
steps.memory_tip: Check: does differentiating your chosen f(x) give the OTHER bracket term exactly? Here d/dx(sinx)=cosx, so f(x)=sinx is correct.

steps.label: Apply the formula for the final answer
steps.why: Substituting f(x)=sinx directly into the standard result ∫eˣ[f+f′]dx = eˣf(x)+c gives the answer immediately — no further integration is needed once f is identified.
common_mistakes: Writing eˣ(sinx+cosx) as the final answer instead of just eˣsinx.
steps.memory_tip: The answer keeps ONLY f(x), never the full bracket — eˣ sinx, not eˣ(sinx+cosx).
